turns.question: Where is the structural map engine implemented, and how is the parser engine selected per file?
turns.text:
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to locate the map/parsing engine.The README points to `internal/mapengine/`. Let me look at the actual routing/selection code.`Map` and `mapAuto` in types.go look like the dispatcher. Let me read the full file for exact logic.I now have full confirmation of the call site and dispatch logic. Here's the answer.

## Structural map engine

**Package:** `internal/mapengine/` (Go, in `gkoreli/ghx`)

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `types.go` | Shared types (`Engine`, `Level`, `Kind`, `Options`, `Result`, `Symbol`), the `Mapper` interface, and the **dispatcher** (`Map`, `mapAuto`, `mapTreeSitterWithFallback`) |
| `goast.go` | `GoASTMapper` — parses `.go` files with Go's own `go/ast` + `go/token` |
| `treesitter.go` | `TreeSitterMapper` — parses via [gotreesitter](https://github.com/odvcencio/gotreesitter) grammars (`grammars.LangEntry`, `gotreesitter.Tagger`/`Tag`) |
| `regex.go` | `RegexMapper` — line-pattern fallback (`regexRules` keyed by extension, `rulesForPath`, `matchLine`) |

It's invoked from `internal/ghx/read.go:187` — when `Read()` sees `opts.Map == true`, it calls `mapengine.Map(path, content, mapengine.Options{Engine: opts.MapEngine, Level: opts.MapLevel, Kind: opts.MapKind})` (the CLI's `--map`, `--level`, `--kind` flags flow into `MapEngine`/`MapLevel`/`MapKind` on that same struct, lines 37–39). No extra GitHub API call is made — it maps content already fetched.

## How the engine is selected per file (`types.go`)

`Map()` (line 125) first normalizes `opts.Engine` via `normalizeEngine` (line 80) — any value that isn't literally `"regex"` or `"tree-sitter"` collapses to `EngineAuto`. Then:

- `EngineRegex` → forces `RegexMapper{}.Map(...)`
- `EngineTreeSitter` → forces `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., warnUnsupported=true)`
- `EngineAuto` (default) → `mapAuto(path, content, opts)`, which switches on `filepath.Ext(path)` (line 143):
  - `.go` → `GoASTMapper{}.Map`; on error, silently falls back to `RegexMapper` (`result.Fallback = true`)
  - `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.py`, `.rs` → `mapTreeSitterWithFallback(..., warnUnsupported=false)`, which tries `TreeSitterMapper{}.Map` and falls back to regex on any error (adding a warning unless the error is `ErrUnsupportedLanguage`)
  - everything else → `RegexMapper{}.Map` directly

So selection is purely by file extension in auto mode, with regex always as the last-resort fallback for parse errors or unsupported languages — matching the README's description ("Go uses `go/ast`; TS/JS/Python/Rust use tree-sitter; everything else falls back to regex").

## What I did not verify
- I did not read `treesitter.go`'s `defaultTreeSitterLanguageConfigs()` body or `grammars` package in detail to confirm exactly which tree-sitter grammar library backs each of the 5 listed languages — only the extension→engine routing and file/function names, via structural maps rather than full source.
- I did not verify `internal/cli` flag wiring (e.g., cobra flag names in `code.go`/`ghx.go`) end-to-end from CLI argument parsing to `read.go`'s `MapEngine` field — I confirmed the read.go call site but not the cobra flag definitions themselves.
- I did not run the code or tests; conclusions rest solely on static reading of `types.go`, `read.go`, and structural maps of `goast.go`/`treesitter.go`/`regex.go`.

README:
# ghx — the code-reconnaissance sidecar for AI agents

**Expensive main agents shouldn't burn frontier tokens on tree/grep/read loops.**
ghx is a cheap, specialized **sidecar agent** that a main agent delegates code
reconnaissance to. Ask it a repo question in plain English; it explores GitHub
under the hood and hands back a **schema-validated evidence report** — claims
with citations, the commands it ran, and what it could not confirm — while every
artifact of the investigation lands on disk under `~/.ghx/sessions/` for you or
the parent agent to inspect.

This is the first public cut of the **Agent Sidecar Framework**: a main agent
delegates a whole competence domain to a proficient specialist instead of loading
that domain's tools and doctrine into its own context. ghx is the proof — the
code-reconnaissance sidecar — and, underneath it, a sharp standalone GitHub
exploration CLI. The durable vision lives in
[docs/NORTH_STAR.md](docs/NORTH_STAR.md).

> ghx is two products in one binary: a **sidecar brain** you delegate to (this
> README's lead), and the **classic exploration CLI** it drives under the hood
> (documented in full further down). Use whichever fits; they share one core.

## Why a sidecar

When a main agent stops mid-task to explore code, the real cost is not the API
calls — it is the context. Exploration output floods the window, the agent loses
the thread of the engineering work, and the ~400 lines of tool
